referents.why: 'Some' (τινες) is an indefinite group not named as a candidate in this verse.
referents.category: indefinite group not offered as candidate

referents.why: 'Us' (ἡμᾶς), the object of 'to say', is the writer's group, the people slandered; no candidate fits. The builder's 'some' is wrong, since the 'us' is the accused, not the accusers.
referents.category: first person group not offered as candidate

referents.why: 'Their' (ὧν) refers back to the slanderers ('some'), who are not a candidate.
referents.category: relative genitive refers to uncandidated group

referents.why: 'We are slandered' (βλασφημούμεθα): the writer's group; no candidate fits.
referents.category: first person group not offered as candidate

referents.why: Hortatory 'let us do' inside the slogan: the 'we' of the accused; no candidate fits.
referents.category: first person group not offered as candidate

links.why: A clause cannot join itself; this is a parser error.
καί ... καθώς: 'and as' joins two comparisons of the same report.
Superseded: the infinitive is the object of 'affirm', a saying, so the content link carries it (R1).
φασίν ('affirm') introduces what is said, 'that we say'; it is the saying clause and its content (R1).
ὧν ('of whom') opens a new sentence after a question mark; it is Paul's verdict on the slanderers, not a relative clause inside cl1.
Superseded: 'to say' (λέγειν) is a saying, so its content link to the slogan is the R1 link.
λέγειν introduces the slogan 'Let us do evil that good may come', its content; nested speech takes its own content link (R1).
ἵνα ('so that') gives the aim of doing evil: that good may come.

groups.why: cl5 is Paul's verdict, not part of the slander, so it leaves the turn. The sender 'some' is not a candidate, so the sender is omitted.
The hortatory 'let us do evil' with its aim 'that good may come': one command with what qualifies it. Content for cl2 goes to the clause cl3, since it is one command.

none_fit.where: cl5 (ὧν τὸ κρίμα ἔνδικόν ἐστιν, 'their condemnation is just')
none_fit.what: A verdict on the slanderers after a sentence break, with a relative genitive back-referring; no link type for a verdict on a group named earlier.
A καθώς ('as') clause hangs from an elided main clause ('why not say'); no host clause is in the verse for an 'as' link.

cant_tell.what: the inner turn 'we say' (cl2) and its sender
cant_tell.why: The sender 'we' is not a candidate, so the nested turn is not built; the content links carry the speech.
